rationale: Both candidates correctly validate the core codes.audio fix, but Y more precisely reproduces the ground-truth reviewer's central non-blocking concern — that the containment fallback silently weakens the escalation guarantee for all callers, not just opt-in ones — backing it with a concrete grep for the one live escalation consumer and a quoted docstring contradiction, whereas X raises a similar but vaguer point without engaging the docstring/escalation-interaction specifically. Y also surfaces an additional, verifiably correct dead-code bug (the unreachable transcript_words/expected_words guard) and a legitimate test-coverage gap (only one of six flagged regression tests was re-run), giving it broader coverage and more concrete, line-anchored directives; X's review is cleaner but shallower and misses the docstring-staleness angle GT emphasized.
